beats.got: I read two real cases, a lawyer and a consultancy report. Those are the kind of public failures a board remembers.

take_homes: Nobody can promise an agent is safe, so you run a check repeatedly and write down what risk is left.
The cheapest control is not connecting the agent to the system in the first place.
Residual risk gets named, accepted by someone on record, and unclear cases go to the person who owns the area, with the evidence.

monday.move: Ask IT and legal what rules apply before my controller tries an agent on month-end variance commentary, and have the controller read-only scope it first

monday.stop_condition: IT has not approved the tool for finance data
monday.blocker: IT approval for finance data. I also still have no cost per month or payback figure for the board.

misconception.why: The reusable check and the written rules look like something the organisation builds and keeps, not a licence. But no cost was ever given, so I only half buy it.

one_line: Honest about risk and I liked the 'accept it on record' part, but there was not one cost figure in the whole module.
